issues.issue: "Confidential Information" is defined by an open-ended list introduced by "including, but not limited to" and closed by "and the like", against the only real limit being information "not generally known in the business community". The reach of the catch-all and the vagueness of that limiting phrase leave the covenant's boundary contestable.

The clause provides that Section 3 "shall survive the termination of this Agreement", but the Agreement contains no term or termination provision at all, so the trigger for survival has no referent. A court could be asked what termination means in an instrument that cannot be terminated.

"Disparage, criticize or make statements to the detriment of any other Party" is vague at the edges — ordinary truthful criticism or commercial statements could fall within it — and the carve-out for "any dispute resolution proceeding related to any Agreement between the Parties" is itself indefinite. Its temporal reach, "while this Agreement is in effect and indefinitely thereafter", also has no defined term to measure against.

The clause supersedes all "prior and contemporaneous agreements" on the subject matter while Background C incorporates definitions from the contemporaneous Stock Purchase Agreement, and it makes the non-party Buyer a third-party beneficiary although Section 2's covenants run to the Company. Whether the Buyer may enforce, and whether the SPA survives as an interpretive source, are questions the two clauses leave unsettled.

The forum provision says actions "may be brought" in the Michigan state or federal courts and each party "consents to the jurisdiction", which is the classic permissive-versus-mandatory ambiguity: it is not clear whether Michigan is the exclusive forum or merely one available forum. With a shareholder resident in India, whether the clause bars a forum non conveniens or jurisdictional challenge is squarely open.

The carve-out lets "the Company" assign to "an affiliate" without consent, but Definitions B already defines "Company" to include its affiliates and successors, so the exception's operation is circular. Whether the Buyer, a non-party beneficiary, is covered by the assignment restriction is likewise unaddressed.

The saving proviso turns on whether deletion would work "such a material change as to cause completion of the transactions contemplated hereby to be unreasonable", a standard that is both vague and misdescribed — this Agreement contemplates no transactions, the Stock Purchase Agreement does. The clause also contains the typo "Wlegality" for "illegality".

The clause cross-refers to "this Section 5(J)" although the Agreement's sections are inconsistently numbered and lettered, and the Company's telephone and facsimile lines are left blank despite facsimile being an authorised delivery method. These are mechanical gaps that could matter to whether a notice was validly given.
